hypotheses.justification: Not needed to elaborate the statement. Over a Noetherian ring R, AdicCompletion I R is flat over R; Mathlib proves this as the instance `flat_of_isNoetherian` via `Module.Flat.iff_lTensor_injective'`, using the finite case of this lemma only for ideal inclusions J →ₗ R, where J and R are finite because R is Noetherian. So keep the current finite version as a private lemma, prove flatness, then for an injective f between arbitrary modules apply `Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/Basic.lean, no finiteness hypotheses) to get `f.lTensor (AdicCompletion I R)` injective. `AlgebraTensorModule.map LinearMap.id f` is the same function as `f.lTensor (AdicCompletion I R)` (both send a ⊗ₜ m to a ⊗ₜ f m; equal by extensionality on the tensor product). The proof needs no finiteness of M, and the theorem stays true even if both finiteness instances are dropped.

Same argument: once AdicCompletion I R is known to be flat over the Noetherian ring R (shown from the ideal case J →ₗ R, which only needs finiteness of J and R), `Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap` gives injectivity of `f.lTensor (AdicCompletion I R)`, which is the same function as `AlgebraTensorModule.map LinearMap.id f`, for any codomain N. N being finite is not needed to elaborate the statement or to prove it. It can be dropped together with [Module.Finite R M].
